Very mixed
Apr 2026 • Family
We decided to test the restaurant ranked #1 on Tripadvisor, which also presents itself as a Belgian establishment. Growing up near the border with our Belgian cousins until I was a teenager, it was an opportunity for me to find some youthful pleasures. Moreover, when I return with my family to the region, I always make a small detour through Belgium.

So here we are in a friendly setting, where we quickly understand that the main theme is beer. A musical atmosphere composed of French songs from the 70s, 80s and 90s reinforces this pleasant feeling of nostalgia. We are located on the first floor, with only one other table occupied.

Very quickly, a waitress comes three times to take our order. However, with such a wide selection of dishes and beers, and what’s more, a menu for two, we need a little time to decide. I try in turn to soothe those few minutes of waiting with a smile... that she will not return to me. Besides, whether it is her or her colleague, no smile will be exchanged throughout the meal.

First problem: the beers we had spotted and praised are all unavailable, due to lack of stock. We therefore fall back on other choices, with flavors sometimes more complex than expected. I take a brunette, my wife a white.

The waitress arrives with the drinks and undertakes to serve the beers herself. I already don’t particularly appreciate being served my beer, let alone in this way. Whether for our table or for others, it pours about three-quarters of the bottle into the glass, then shakes the rest vigorously to recover any deposits and yeasts at the bottom, before pouring them also. It is worth remembering that not all beers contain deposits, that not all yeasts are necessarily pleasant to taste, and that not all customers necessarily want to find them in their glass.

Let's move on to food. I had invited my daughter, who had been living in Ho Chi Minh City for some time, and who dreamed of tasting cheese — a relatively hard-to-find commodity to find there. The old maps included Trappist cheese, but this was replaced by the much vaguer reference to “European cheese”. A name that puzzles, a bit like simply offering “European wine”.

My daughter therefore asks the waitress for details on the variety and origin of cheeses. She's unable to answer and goes off to find out... without ever coming back. Another waitress finally comes by and asks her again. Answer: “goat”, without further details. Finally, once served, the cheese advertised as goat turns out to be cow cheese. As for smoked cheese, it turns out to be simply salty, difficult to identify and without real taste. We will never know the origin of these cheeses, but one thing is certain: it was not trappist, and that is probably why the mention disappeared from the map.

For my part, I had opted for “Belgium fries”. The title is promising and assumed — where we usually speak of “French fries” in English. So I expected to find the famous Belgian fries, cooked in beef fat with double cooking. On arrival, the disappointment is clear: nothing recalls the real Belgian fries. They are not bad, but remain very much of a thing. I even wonder if they are not frozen. A bánh mì vendor in Vung Tau, at Mr Mick’s, offers fries much closer to the Belgian tradition than those served here.

My wife, who had a small appetite, had ordered a rice sautéed with eggs. Again, the dish proved less tasty than those found in local street food.

After paying the bill, we go down to the ground floor and pass the team of waitresses, all without exception gathered on their mobile phones. Maybe they were still looking for the origin of the cheese... 😉 One of them gets up to walk us back to the door.

In the end, I can hardly explain this first place on Tripadvisor. Unless customers don’t really have a point of comparison with a real Belgian brewery in Belgium...

Nevertheless, I prefer to think that it was a simple empty passage for this establishment that evening.
